name: domiciledb
description: Self-hosted home inventory built to prove what you owned and get paid after a disaster.

comments.overrides: Security floors are RANGES (^), never exact pins: npm applies an override verbatim, so an exact version is a ceiling that holds the tree on a known-vulnerable release (brace-expansion@5 sat on 5.0.8 after 5.0.9 shipped for exactly this reason). The @emnapi/* entries below are the one exception and stay exact on purpose. Pin @emnapi/* (optional+peer wasm deps from sharp/transitive) to consistent versions; works around an npm bug where the lockfile writer and `npm ci` validator disagree, which otherwise breaks `npm ci` in CI and Docker. brace-expansion@1/@5 and sharp are pinned to their fixed releases for GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp (ReDoS) and GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj (libvips runtime CVEs); the sharp override also lifts next's bundled 0.34.x copy past the vuln. brace-expansion@5 floors at ^5.0.9 for GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (unbounded expand() output -> uncatchable OOM); that advisory covers everything <=5.0.7 with no backport to the 1.x line, so brace-expansion@1 floors at ^1.1.16 (resolving 1.1.18) and stays on the 1.x line, suppressed in osv-scanner.toml -- it is dev-only (ESLint 9's minimatch@3) and cannot be lifted, because brace-expansion 5 replaced the callable CommonJS default export with a named `expand`, which makes minimatch@3 throw at require time.
